Last week I was in Dubai for
UiPath
FUSION, held at the Museum of the Future. Over the past ten years of visiting, I have seen a pace of development here that few places in the world can match. What stands out is the openness to embrace new technology, not for its own sake, but to make people’s lives better and public services more efficient.

That openness shaped our conversations at FUSION. With customers and partners from across the region, I focused on accountability and how the role of people changes as organizations delegate more work to AI. The question is no longer only what AI can do, but who answers for what it does.

Our customers are already facing this question. We heard from
etisalat
about their automation journey, and leaders from
Etihad
,
Power International Holding
,
Dubai Health
and
Mediclinic Group
joined a panel on AI transformation across the public and private sectors.

They talked about moving from isolated pilots to AI that runs inside core operations that impact their customers and patients. In industries this regulated and sensitive, they were clear that governance and trust matter as much as the technology.

Thank you to everyone who joined us in Dubai.

3 days at
UiPath
FUSION 2026 in Las Vegas. Everything I saw, in 1 video. The theme was “Where AI meets ROI.” After 3 days on the floor, I think UiPath backed it up. The announcements:

1. Cartographer
Builds a Map of Work through a guided conversation. The rules, exceptions and judgment calls sitting in people’s heads become build-ready specs. The Decision Ledger ties every change to an owner’s approval.

2. Faster building
UiPath Coding Agents are GA. Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and Antigravity work with UiPath too. Delegate takes care of admin and role-specific tasks.

3. Connected data
Integration Service adds Database Hub, Relay for on-prem and an MCP Connector. Data Fabric gives agents governed context from Salesforce and SAP with zero-copy Federated Entities.

4. Governance at every layer
1 policy framework for agents, robots and people. Runtime Checker validates agents while they run. Compliance Packs and LLM-as-Judge guardrails sit on top.

5. The dark testing factory
Test Cloud adds Autopilot, Autonomous Exploration, Playwright integration and testing for AI agents.

The conversations:
Michael Atalla
, CMO
How you explain a Map of Work to a CFO who only wants ROI, and why UiPath opened its platform to other coding agents.
Vikram Kakumani
, Deputy CTO
The move from RPA to agentic automation, controlled agency, and how Maestro orchestrates agents, robots and people together.
Manas Khemani
, Banking and Financial Services
Agentic AI already live in production with customers, in one of the most regulated industries out there.

Also in the video: a live demo of a healthcare payer automating fax processing end to end, plus pre-built industry solution kits.

My take:
The hardest part of enterprise AI is context. How does the work actually run? Who approves the change? What happens when an agent gets it wrong?
UiPath is answering all 3 in 1 platform. Map the work. Build faster. Govern at runtime.

Thank you to the UiPath team for having me as a partner this year. See you at the next one.
Which of these would you put to work first?

UiPath FUSION München is a wrap. Thank you to all our customers, partners and the awesome UiPathers!!
On Wednesday we filled the Sofitel Bayerpost to talk about one thing: where AI meets ROI. Not the hype. What’s actually running in production.

I opened with UiPath offering 'Controlled Agency' - allowing the best of Deterministic and Autonomous in a workflow. The role of ''the Builder of Bots'' has now evolved into ''The Architect of Work''. 

A few moments that stuck with me:
🔹
Raghu Malpani
on what’s new and what’s next across the UiPath Platform, followed by
George Barnett
on finding your path to the Map of Work.
🔹 The
Dark Testing Factory
hosted by
Gerrit Knippschild
with
Johannes Reitermayer
(LGT),
Pierluigi Mega
(Merck) and
Thomas Stocker
: a self-operating quality system, with people still setting the direction.
🔹
Wojciech Szremski
on building the foundation for scalable AI agents at Schaeffler.
🔹
Michiel van den Berg
and
Heiko Bischoff
on HARIBO’s recipe for intelligent automation with real ROI.
🔹
Michael Noll
(AOK Baden-Württemberg) and
Tim Zimmermann
(Roboyo) on AOK’s first agentic use case in production: the agent reviews, humans decide.
🔹 Justin Klemme and
Jonas Alexander Schmidt
showing how TiMo at Rossmann assesses defects and notifies landlords automatically.
🔹
Neil Ward-Dutton
(IDC) closing with an honest look at agentic AI today and what to do about it.

Huge thanks as well to
Linda Xiang
&
Michael Grimm
(Capgemini / MAN Truck & Bus),
Ingmar Helmers
&
Joana Hermann
(cronos / Aurubis),
Samuel Porter
(Kantonsspital Graubünden),
Ferhat Datli
&
Fassih Fariwar
(M-net / Lunatec) and
Florian Huber
(Swisscom). Your stories are why people came!!

The day was a blur. Dozens of meetings, in rooms, corridors, during lunch or coffee... the place buzzed. UiPath's Map of Work was the centerstage for the buzz and what UiPath/Partners can do to make it all happen.

See you all next year!
